name: Discriminative evaluation — designed to decide between hypotheses, not to demonstrate the method
Belief-change — the output is a changed understanding rather than a delivered artifact
Cost stated TOGETHER WITH gain, so the trade is checkable
Limiting result stated TOGETHER WITH the conditions under which it holds
Hedging-word density
Theory and experiment coupled — the experiments test the theory's own prediction
Explicit priority or first-ness claims
Precise delta — prior work is characterised specifically enough that the change is checkable
Derivation coupling — the problem's structure is established first and the method is derived from it
Generality of the formal statement TOGETHER WITH concreteness of its instantiation
Syntactic complexity independent of total length
Rhetorical questions posed in the abstract
Restraint — claim language is calibrated BELOW what the reported results would license
Non-idiomatic English and grammatical slips
Membership in the privacy / security / adversarial-robustness subfield
Subsumption — prior work is exhibited as special cases of a more general statement
Reusable artifact — what is left behind is fit for others to build on, judged scale-free
Mechanistic explanation of an OBSERVED fact, not of the proposed method
Simplicity of the solution RELATIVE TO the difficulty of the problem it solves
Names and characterises a phenomenon that did not previously have a name
Insight portability — the finding would survive replacing the specific benchmark it was shown on
First-person narrative density
Typographic emphasis used inside the abstract
Acronym density
Inline author-year citations inside the abstract
